dedupe_keys.name: vesselfinder ais station network and coverage map

description: VesselFinder's AIS station pages show the network of shore-based Automatic Identification System receivers that feed its vessel tracking service, with a live map of where stations are online or offline. Coverage: worldwide; the map showed 1,475 stations online when read. Contents: each partner station gets an identifier and a public page with its performance, such as vessels tracked, coverage range and activity, and owners get alerts if a station stops reporting. Anyone with a receiver can apply by sending equipment and location; VesselFinder replies with forwarding settings, and partners receive a free Premium account. Format and access: an interactive web map and station pages; no bulk download was seen. Licence and cost: free to view under VesselFinder's terms; no open licence. Caveats: coverage depends on volunteers, so gaps are uneven, and range figures are per station, not a modelled coverage surface. The station map shows where AIS reception, and so vessel observation, is reliable, which helps judge data gaps in hazard exposure and traffic flow studies built on AIS. It relates to the AISHub data exchange and the VesselFinder port calls API in the catalogue.
